portName: King's Wharf and Heritage Wharf, Royal Naval Dockyard
townName: the Dockyard, with Hamilton and St George's by ferry
seoTitle: Bermuda cruise port guide: Dockyard, Hamilton, St George's
seoDescription: Bermuda cruise port 2026: ships dock at Royal Naval Dockyard. Ferry to Hamilton 15–25 min, St George's about 45 min. 1-day bus and ferry pass BD$19 (2026).
quickAnswer: Ships dock alongside at King's Wharf or Heritage Wharf in the Royal Naval Dockyard, at the island's western tip; there is no tender. The Dockyard is walkable, but Hamilton is about 24 km away, so take the Blue Route ferry (15–25 minutes) and the Orange Route ferry for St George's (about 45 minutes, limited sailings). A 1-day pass for all buses and ferries costs BD$19 (2026). Be on a ferry leaving Hamilton 2 hours before all-aboard and on one leaving St George's 2.5 hours before.
intro: Bermuda's cruise berths sit in the old Royal Navy base at the far western end of the island. The Dockyard itself is compact, with a fort museum, a beach and shops on foot, but the island's two towns and the south-shore beaches all need a ferry, a bus or a taxi. Ferries are the fast way to Hamilton and St George's, and the public bus reaches Horseshoe Bay. The government expected 194 cruise calls between March and November 2026, with more weekend calls than before, and some ships stay overnight. Check your itinerary: a two-day call changes what is realistic.

terminals.name: King's Wharf
terminals.notes: Main cruise pier in the Dockyard, with its own terminal building selling souvenirs, tourist information and transport passes. Taxi ranks are outside the port. Distance shown is to Hamilton.

terminals.name: Heritage Wharf
terminals.notes: Second Dockyard pier, usually one ship per pier. Same ferry dock, taxis and walking routes. Distance shown is to Hamilton.

walkability.detail: Everything in the Dockyard is within walking distance; the area is less than a mile end to end. The National Museum of Bermuda and Snorkel Park Beach are about 10 minutes from the ship, the Clocktower Mall about 10 minutes the other way. Hamilton, St George's and the south-shore beaches are not walkable.

transportSections.cost: Cash BD$3.50–5.00 by zone, exact change, no notes; tokens BD$2.75–4.50 (2026)
transportSections.detail: Fast ferry from the Dockyard ferry dock, beside the cruise terminals. Check departure times posted at the dock or in the Summer 2026 schedule. Extra sailings on Wednesday evenings in summer for Harbour Nights.

transportSections.mode: Orange Route ferry to St George's
transportSections.cost: Covered by a transportation pass; tokens or cash as above (2026)
transportSections.detail: Direct Dockyard to St George's service restored from 6 April 2026, two or three sailings a day on selected days. First departure from the Dockyard 09:30; last departure from St George's 18:00. Read the return times before you board.

transportSections.cost: 1 day BD$19, 2 days BD$31.50, 3 days BD$44 adult; child 5–16 BD$9.50 for 1 day (2026)
transportSections.detail: Unlimited buses and ferries. Sold at the Dockyard Visitor Information Centre (tokens and passes), the Hamilton Ferry Terminal and on the government's Shorelink app.

transportSections.cost: BD$3.50 (3 zones) or BD$5.00 (14 zones) cash; or pass (2026)
transportSections.detail: Route 7 links the Dockyard with Horseshoe Bay, Gibbs Hill Lighthouse, Elbow Beach, the Botanical Gardens and Hamilton. Pink stop poles mean the bus is heading to Hamilton; blue poles mean away from it. Drivers give no change and do not take notes.

transportSections.time: About 20 min to Horseshoe Bay; about 30 min to Hamilton
transportSections.detail: Taxi ranks are outside the port. Most taxis seat up to seven, and they can also be booked through the Hitch or BTOA Connect apps. Tourists cannot rent ordinary cars.

returnTiming.rule: Be on a ferry leaving Hamilton by 15:30 and on one leaving St George's by 15:00 for a 17:30 all-aboard. Leave Horseshoe Bay by 15:30.
returnTiming.detail: The Hamilton ferry takes 15–25 minutes, but you may wait for the next sailing, and you need to be on board 60 minutes before all-aboard. The St George's ferry takes about 45 minutes and runs only two or three times a day, so a missed boat can leave you with no direct sailing in time. The bus from Hamilton takes 45–60 minutes. From Horseshoe Bay a taxi takes about 20 minutes, but buses run on a timetable you need to check.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: Take a taxi to the Dockyard; from Hamilton allow about 30 minutes, and longer from St George's at the other end of the island. If you will miss all-aboard, call the port agent number on your ship's daily programme at once.

excursionAdvice: For Hamilton, skip the ship tour: the ferry is quick and covered by the day pass. St George's is the borderline case. The direct ferry takes about 45 minutes, but there are only two or three sailings a day on selected days, so on a single-day call with an early all-aboard a ship tour removes the timing risk. Beach transfers to Horseshoe Bay are convenient but not necessary if you are happy to use the bus or share a taxi. On an overnight call, do St George's on your own and keep the ship tours for the things you cannot reach easily.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes the ship docks at 08:00 at King's Wharf or Heritage Wharf and all-aboard is 17:30. A Hamilton and Horseshoe Bay day on a 1-day pass.

steps.what: Off the ship. Buy a 1-day transportation pass (BD$19) at the Dockyard Visitor Information Centre and note the Blue Route ferry times.
Blue Route ferry to Hamilton, 15–25 minutes, or the next sailing after it.
Explore Hamilton on foot: the harbourfront and the city streets.
Route 7 bus from Hamilton along the South Shore towards the Dockyard. Get off at Horseshoe Bay.
Leave Horseshoe Bay by route 7 bus towards the Dockyard, or by taxi (about 20 minutes). Leave by 15:30 at the latest.
Back in the Dockyard. Short walk around the Clocktower Mall or a drink near the pier.
Back on board, 60 minutes before all-aboard.

sights.name: National Museum of Bermuda
sights.why: The island's largest fort, now a museum of about 500 years of Bermuda history including shipwreck finds.
sights.cost: Not verified; check at the gate
sights.tip: About 10 minutes' walk from the ship. A good choice for the last hours of the day, close to the gangway.

sights.name: Royal Naval Dockyard
sights.why: The former Royal Navy base, used until 1951, with stone storehouses, the Clocktower Mall and the Bermuda Craft Market.
sights.tip: Much of the area closes early, even when ships stay overnight.

sights.name: Snorkel Park Beach
sights.why: Small man-made beach in a protected cove, the closest place to swim from the ship.
sights.tip: About 10 minutes' walk from the ship. Useful when you want to stay close to the gangway.

sights.name: Hamilton
sights.tip: Take the Blue Route ferry; it is much quicker than the 45–60 minute bus.

sights.name: St George's
sights.why: Bermuda's old town at the east end of the island.
sights.tip: Orange Route ferry, about 45 minutes, from 09:30. Plan your return sailing before you go; there are only two or three a day.

sights.name: Horseshoe Bay
sights.why: South Shore beach on bus route 7, with a snack bar and chair hire.
sights.tip: Bus route 7 stops there, or take a taxi of about 20 minutes.

sights.name: Gibbs Hill Lighthouse
sights.why: Lighthouse in Southampton, on bus route 7 between the Dockyard and Hamilton.
sights.tip: Combine with Horseshoe Bay on the same bus route.

sights.name: Bermuda Botanical Gardens
sights.why: Gardens near Hamilton, on bus route 7.
sights.tip: Fits a Hamilton day if you return by ferry.

beaches.note: Man-made beach in a protected cove; chairs and gear for hire.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming Hamilton is walkable from the ship.
commonMistakes.fix: It is about 24 km away. Take the Blue Route ferry, 15–25 minutes.

commonMistakes.mistake: Taking the ferry to St George's without checking the return sailings.
commonMistakes.fix: There are only two or three a day. Read the timetable at the Dockyard and be on a boat leaving St George's 2.5 hours before all-aboard.

commonMistakes.mistake: Trying to pay the bus with a banknote.
commonMistakes.fix: Buses take exact coins, tokens or passes only. Buy a pass or tokens at the Dockyard first.

commonMistakes.mistake: Taking the bus to Hamilton instead of the ferry.
commonMistakes.fix: The bus takes 45–60 minutes; the ferry 15–25. Use the bus for beaches, not for Hamilton.

commonMistakes.mistake: Waiting at the wrong side of the road for a bus.
commonMistakes.fix: Pink poles are for buses towards Hamilton, blue poles for buses away from it.

safety: Bermuda is safe for visitors, and the Dockyard is calm by day and night. The main risks are on the roads and in the sea. Some roads near the Dockyard have no pavement, so take a taxi rather than walking to beaches outside it, such as Sea Glass Beach. Swim where lifeguards are on duty and follow their flags.
accessibility: Ships berth alongside, so there is no tender. The Dockyard is compact and mostly level. Ferries have wheelchair roll-on, roll-off access at the Dockyard, Hamilton, St George's and Rockaway, and the two new ferries introduced in 2026 were described as more accessible. Buses are not fully accessible: they kneel, and some carry folded wheelchairs, but none have ramps. Some taxis are wheelchair accessible; ask when booking.
rainyDay: Stay in the Dockyard: the National Museum of Bermuda takes a couple of hours, and the Clocktower Mall and Craft Market are under cover. Hamilton by ferry also works in rain, as the crossing is short and the town is compact. Avoid St George's on a wet single-day call, as the ferry ride is long and sailings are few.
crowdTips: The government expected 194 cruise calls from March to November 2026, with more on weekends than in past years. When two ships are in, queues form for passes, taxis and the first ferries. Buy a pass at once or the evening before on an overnight call, and take an early ferry.

faqs.a: No. Large ships dock alongside at King's Wharf or Heritage Wharf in the Royal Naval Dockyard.

faqs.q: Is Hamilton walkable from the Bermuda cruise port?
faqs.a: No. Hamilton is about 24 km from the Dockyard. The Blue Route ferry takes 15–25 minutes.

faqs.q: How do I get from the Dockyard to St George's?
faqs.a: By the Orange Route ferry, about 45 minutes, restored as a direct service from April 2026. It runs two or three times a day on selected days; check the return times before you go.

faqs.q: How much is the Bermuda bus and ferry pass?
faqs.a: BD$19 for one day, BD$31.50 for two and BD$44 for three, adult, 2026. It covers all buses and ferries.

faqs.q: Can I pay the Bermuda bus in US dollars?
faqs.a: The Bermuda dollar is at par with the US dollar. Buses take exact change in coins only, no notes, so buy tokens or a pass first.

faqs.q: How do I get to Horseshoe Bay from the cruise port?
faqs.a: Bus route 7, or a taxi of about 20 minutes.

faqs.q: What can I do in Bermuda in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: Ferry to Hamilton, bus to Horseshoe Bay for a swim, and back to the Dockyard by 15:30–16:00. Or stay local: the National Museum and Snorkel Park Beach.
Yes. Take a taxi where roads have no pavement, and swim at lifeguarded beaches.
